summary: Replaced the plain device list with the card-based dashboard grid from the design reference, wired to live snapshot data. Each DeviceCard shows connection status, CPU/MEM/DISK/TEMP mini bars with the same warning/offline thresholds as the mockup, an offline banner with last-seen time, uptime/container/last-refresh footer, and Terminal (disabled until WU016)/Services/Refresh actions. A new useDeviceSnapshots hook loads each device's last-known snapshot on mount and stays live via the existing device://snapshot-updated event. Refresh All and per-card Refresh both call the already-async WU011 monitoring commands. Frontend-only; 152 backend tests unaffected.
completed: features/dashboard/DeviceCard.tsx: status dot (pulses when online), name/type badge/hostname, offline/error banner with relative last-seen time, 4-column CPU/MEM/DISK/TEMP bars (dimmed via opacity when snapshot.stale, carrying forward WU011's stale-data-stays-visible behavior), uptime/container-count/last-refresh footer, Terminal (disabled with a 'not wired up yet' tooltip since open_device_terminal doesn't exist until WU016)/Services/Refresh action row. Entire card is clickable and keyboard-accessible (Enter/Space) to open device detail; action buttons stop propagation.
stores/useDeviceSnapshots.ts: fetches get_latest_snapshot per device on mount, subscribes to device://snapshot-updated for the component's lifetime, returns a live Record<deviceId, DeviceSnapshot>.

features/dashboard/DashboardScreen.tsx: renders the card grid, adds a Refresh All button (refresh_all_devices) and wires each card's Refresh button (refresh_device); kept Edit/Delete as compact buttons below each card since Device Detail's settings-gear edit entry point doesn't exist until WU014 -- removing them now would have made devices uneditable for a work unit.

lib/formatting/{uptime,relativeTime,metricThresholds,deviceMetrics}.ts: small pure formatting helpers (seconds -> '14d 6h', ISO timestamp -> '5 min ago', percent/temp -> threshold color class, metrics -> memory/disk percent).
Verified npm run build and npm run lint (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings) pass; cargo test still 152/152 (untouched by this frontend-only work unit).

validationCommands.summary: TypeScript build succeeds with the new components/hooks/helpers.
0 errors, 3 pre-existing HMR-granularity warnings (unrelated to this WU).
152/152 unit tests passed, unaffected (no backend changes this WU).

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Dashboard shows a card per device with live status and metrics
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DeviceCard renders status dot/metrics/footer from useDeviceSnapshots, which is backed by get_latest_snapshot + the device://snapshot-updated event confirmed emitted in the WU011/WU012 backend.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Offline/stale devices are visually distinguishable from healthy ones
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Offline banner (WifiOff icon + status label + last-seen) renders whenever snapshot exists but connectionStatus != online; stale carried-forward metrics render at opacity-60 per metricThresholds/DeviceCard.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Refresh actions (single device and all devices) are reachable from the dashboard
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Refresh All button calls refreshAllDevices; each card's Refresh icon button calls refreshDevice(id), both showing a spinner while in flight via refreshingIds/refreshingAll state.

notes: Risk score: 10/100 (low). Rationale: purely additive frontend work consuming already-tested backend commands/events; no new backend surface, no persistence changes.

Terminal button is intentionally disabled -- open_device_terminal is WU016 scope. Edit/Delete were deliberately kept on the dashboard rather than removed, since Device Detail (WU014) doesn't yet provide an alternative entry point.

Could not capture a visual screenshot of the rendered dashboard this session -- the user's desktop was in active fullscreen use both times checked, and forcing window focus over that felt like the wrong call. Verified instead via a clean TypeScript build plus a live smoke test confirming state.json's snapshot shape matches exactly what useDeviceSnapshots expects from the backend event.
